review: This is the tour that answers the real question behind "Jewish Quarter tour Budapest": can I get inside the synagogues without sorting tickets myself? Yes. The price includes entry to the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street, the restored Rumbach Street Synagogue, the Holocaust Memorial Park and the Orthodox Kazinczy Street Synagogue, with skip-the-line entry at Dohány.

The route covers the full historic district in 2.5 hours: the Neolog community at Dohány, the Righteous Gentiles who saved tens of thousands of Hungarian Jews, at the Wallenberg Memorial Park, Otto Wagner's 1872 Rumbach synagogue, Király utca and Gozsdu udvar, the Carl Lutz Memorial, then Dob utca, the core of the former ghetto, to Kazinczy, the centre of Orthodox life today.

At €55, about €22 per hour, it costs €10 more than the tour with the Jewish Museum (#2), which swaps Rumbach and Kazinczy for the museum. Pick this one if you want the architecture and the living community; pick #2 if you want the museum collection. It is also one of only two options listed as both wheelchair- and pushchair-accessible.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Opening Hours, Dress Code and What Costs Extra
guide.html:
Opening hours. The official hours given in the #9 listing: from 2 November to 31 December 2026 the Dohány Street Synagogue opens Sunday–Thursday 10:00–16:00 (last admission 15:00) and Friday 10:00–14:00 (last admission 13:00). It is closed on Saturday. Plan any tour with synagogue entry for a weekday and book a morning slot on Fridays.

Dress code. Dohány is a working synagogue. Shoulders and knees must be covered, and men cover their heads; a kippah is provided at the entrance. Covers can be bought on site at Dohány if you arrive in shorts, but it is easier to dress for it.

Bags and ID. Some tours ask for a passport or ID card and do not allow luggage or large bags. Several tours do not allow flash photography.

What costs extra. On the exterior-only walks (#4, #5) and the historian tour (#7), synagogue entry is not in the price; the historian tour lists the Dohány ticket at 14,500 Ft. No tour here includes hotel pick-up as standard.

Access. #1, #3, #4 and #9 are listed as wheelchair-accessible. #2 and #6 are not suitable for wheelchair users.

Make a day of it. The quarter is also the city's nightlife district. See our pub crawls for the evening, food tours if you want to taste Budapest's kitchens with a guide, and walking tours for the rest of the city. For the communist era and the Cold War, compare the communist history tours.

faqs.q: Do I need a tour to visit the Dohány Street Synagogue?
faqs.a: No, but a tour solves the two hard parts: the ticket queue and the context. The priority-entry visit from €40 includes skip-the-line entry, a 45-minute guided visit and the Jewish Museum. For Dohány plus Rumbach and Kazinczy in one go, the 2.5-hour walk with 4 entries from €55 is the most complete.

faqs.q: How much are Dohány Street Synagogue tickets with a guide?
faqs.a: Guided options with entry start at €40 (45-minute guided visit plus the Jewish Museum), €45 (tour with the Jewish Museum and Memorial Park), €49 (private tour) and €55 (four entries including Rumbach and Kazinczy). The official fast-track tour in 8 languages is €65.

faqs.q: Is the Dohány Street Synagogue open on Saturday?
faqs.a: No. In November and December 2026 it opens Sunday–Thursday 10:00–16:00 and Friday 10:00–14:00, and is closed on Saturday. Book tours with synagogue entry for another day.

faqs.q: What should I wear to the synagogue?
faqs.a: Cover your shoulders and knees. Men must cover their heads; a kippah is provided at the entrance. Covers can be bought on site at Dohány.

faqs.q: Is there a Jewish Quarter tour in German or Hebrew?
faqs.a: Yes. The official fast-track Dohány tour runs in English, Spanish, Italian, French, German, Russian, Hebrew and Hungarian. The other tours compared here run in English, with French, Spanish or Russian on some.

faqs.q: Which tour includes the Rumbach and Kazinczy synagogues?
faqs.a: The 2.5-hour walk with 4 entries (from €55) includes entry to both, plus Dohány and the Holocaust Memorial Park. The tour with the Jewish Museum includes Rumbach only on its 4-hour option. Most cheaper walks show both from outside.

faqs.q: Can I combine the Jewish Quarter with the ruin bars?
faqs.a: Yes. The ruin bars, street art and Jewish Quarter tour (from €63, 18+) mixes district history with ruin bar stops, and the €3 Past & Present walk ends inside Szimpla Kert. For a full night out, see our pub crawl comparison.

methodology: We compared 9 of Budapest's most popular Jewish Quarter and Dohány Street Synagogue tours on which sites you enter (Dohány, the Jewish Museum, Rumbach, Kazinczy, the Memorial Park), skip-the-line access, length, price per hour, group format, languages and accessibility, using live prices for a normal date in November 2026. Where the same operator sold a longer version of the same tour, we kept the one that suits most visitors and noted the other.
